text:
kai: Heads up — after the 6.5 kernel rollout in eu-west2 we are seeing a set of hosts (p4/p4d pool) where the GPU driver never finishes initializing, host OOMs, and jobs get silently evicted. ~35% capacity in the pool impacted.

sophie: ugh. which images? is this the 6.5.0-rc image?

kai: rolling images built from amzn-6.5.x branch, kernel v6.5.3. CUDA driver stack is CUDA-12.2 + nvidia-driver 530. repo: eu-west2-gpu-rolling.

matt: symptoms? dmesg / journal snippets?

kai: paste of recent dmesg from one host:

```
[  12.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  12.346910] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: nvlink: link down, PCIe training reset
[  12.347222] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: probe of 0000:3b:00.0 failed with error -22
[  12.347500] kernel: cgroup: memory: kill process 2345 (some-runner) score 1237 or sacrifice child
[  12.348000] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (some-runner) total-vm:3200000kB, anon-rss:3100000kB
```

kai: `journalctl -k` shows repeated `probe failed with error -22` across ~20 hosts. `modprobe nvidia` returns `init_module: Invalid argument` on some.

leila: do we see `nvidia_uvm` or `nvidia_drm` failing first?

kai: `nvidia_uvm` mostly loads but then other modules fail to bind to the device. Some hosts show `pci 0000:3b:00.0: couldn't disable ASPM` warnings.

chris: hit the same on a canary yesterday but it recovered after `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` — any transient race?

kai: we've tried module reloads, kernel panic occurs in 2 hosts after reloads. There are also repeated NCCL handshake timeouts in app logs which correlate with the nodes reporting nvlink resets.

matt: capacity math — 35% down means queued capacity backpressure. provisioner is spinning up fallbacks in us-east but that spikes cost by like 40% for the week. Need rollback or hotfix ASAP.

infra-bot: [ALERT] 20 hosts in eu-west2 reported GPU probe failures in the last 10m. Latency impact: high. Ticket created: INFRA-4321.

sophie: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause kernel rollout 2) mark affected hosts unschedulable 3) create a canary image pinned to 5.15 for safe pool 4) if necessary rollback image for eu-west2 to previous AMI.

leila: agree. Also validate dkms and signed modules flags — 6.x changed the module param validation in our build pipeline, could be causing `init_module` invalid arg errors. Are we building modules with CONFIG_MODULE_SIG or forced verifiers?

kai: build config shows module signing enabled, but our signing key changed in the pipeline last week. Could be mismatch.

matt: we should also check for PCI firmware mismatch and NVLink firmware versions — some P4s got older firmware during last provision run. NVLINK handshake plus kernel param validation might produce these errors.

chris: quick triage steps I ran: `dkms status` -> clean, `modinfo nvidia` -> shows version 530.41, `nvidia-smi` fails with "failed to initialize NVML: driver/library version mismatch" on 6 hosts.

kai: exact app impact: several training clusters hit NCCL allreduce stalls; jobs either time out or get rescheduled to other regions. Customer visible slowdown for two accounts that are latency-sensitive.

sophie: action plan for next hour: 1) halt eu-west2 kernel rollout (ops) 2) cordon affected hosts and evacuate workloads (sre-oncall + infra) 3) create a 10-host canary image using 5.15 (build infra) 4) apply kernel pinning on autoscaler to avoid launching new 6.5 nodes in eu-west2 (provisioning team) 5) start rollback AMI build if we can't identify a module signing bug quickly.

ops: already paused the rollout pipeline. mark nodes unschedulable? I can push a script to cordon hosts with `probe failed` in dmesg.

matt: please also set nnf (no-new-fleet) flag on autoscaler so we don't rotate capacity into eu-west2. We've started diverting queued workloads to us-east; cost alert sent to finance.

leila: for root cause, we should compare the module build logs between the last known-good image and the 6.5 image. look for `objtool` errors and `modpost` warnings. Also double-check our kernel headers version when building the module — if headers don't match exact minor kernel, you get weird probe failures.

kai: I'm attaching the build hash for the failing image: `ami-0b7c6f-6.5.3-build-20260301` and the working image `ami-0a1d2c-5.15.21-build-20260208`.

chris: can we triage a single host with `strace` on `modprobe` to see syscall failing arg? may be subtle. If `init_module` is EINVAL it usually means bad ELF or signature mismatch.

matt: ops, schedule a rollback window if we can't confirm quick fix. Need comms with sales/support for affected customers.

infra-bot: [TASK] Created infra runbook draft: `eu-west2-kernel-6.5-gpu-probe-mitigation.md` in /runbooks. Assigned to kai/leila.

sophie: for longer-term: add kernel ABI validation to our CI: after building modules, run `modinfo` and `modprobe --dry-run` in a kernel VM to validate probe path. Also add nvlink stress test in the staging fleet before rollout.

kai: updates in 35m: paused rollout early enough — new instances stopped. We've cordoned 22 hosts and evacuated 18 successfully. One host experienced a kernel panic during evacuation and was marked for rebuild. Current impacted capacity down to ~18% after evacuations.

leila: I'll diff module build artifacts and look for signature key mismatch. If that's it we can re-sign modules with the new key and publish a patched AMI without a full kernel rollback.

matt: please estimate cost delta for fallback region usage this week so we can inform finance. Rough numbers: +$28k if we keep shifted capacity for 7 days.

sophie: update: creating canary pool (10 hosts) on 5.15 now. If canary passes nvlink stress and NCCL tests we'll gradually move jobs back.

kai: thanks. tagging @support for customer comms later. Any other ideas?

chris: also check for userspace libraries mismatch — driver/library mismatch can surface as probe failures in some cases. ensure `libnvidia-ml.so` from the CUDA runtime matches kernel module version.

ops: cordon script pushed: `for h in $(list-failed-hosts); do ocp cordon $h && drain $h --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done` — running now. progress printed in infra dashboard.

sophie: keeping this thread as single source of truth. we'll move to incident channel if customer impact escalates. :handshake:
